summary: AgriSense is an AI-powered crop suitability analyzer that makes NASA Earth data usable for farmers. A user enters a location, a crop and a time window, or asks any farming question in plain language. A team of AI agents then finds the location’s coordinates, pulls daily climate data from NASA POWER (temperature, humidity, rainfall, solar radiation, wind and soil moisture) and returns a clear verdict on whether the crop is suitable, with alternative crops when it isn’t. Raw climate data is technical and hard to interpret, and a wrong crop choice can cost a whole season. AgriSense turns NASA satellite-derived data into practical, location-specific advice anyone can read. A live activity feed shows each step the agents take, so the analysis is transparent.
details:
What it does: AgriSense has two modes. Crop Analysis takes a location, a crop and a duration (a slider sets the number of days) and returns a suitability report. Custom Query answers free-form agriculture and climate questions using real data. Each report includes the location and coordinates, a NASA climate summary (averages, totals, trends), a climate analysis, a suitability verdict and alternative crops.

How it works: A CrewAI hierarchical crew coordinates three agents. A Location Finder geocodes the place with Geopy and Nominatim. A Climate Data Analyst calls the NASA POWER daily API (AG community) for these parameters: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, WS2M, T2MDEW, GWETTOP, GWETROOT and GWETPROF. An Agricultural Research Manager orchestrates the work and the language model writes the final recommendation.

Benefits and impact: The app turns complex NASA data into plain-language decisions and works for any location on Earth. It is transparent, since the live feed shows every tool call. Farmers, students and agricultural planners can use it to make climate-informed crop choices, including in water-limited regions such as Thar, Sindh (your default example).

Tools: Python, Flet (UI), CrewAI, Gemma 4 (via Google AI Studio or via Ollama), Kaggle notebook with Pinggy tunnel, Geopy, Pandas, Requests, NASA POWER API.

Creativity: The app lets you choose the AI backend. You can use Google AI Studio, or run Gemma 4 with Ollama on a free Kaggle GPU and expose it through a Pinggy tunnel, which keeps costs low. Agents use real tools instead of guessing, and the user sees the agents working in real time.

Factors considered: Data accuracy (missing NASA values of -999 are cleaned), flexible date handling, accessibility for non-experts, and low-cost deployment.
